name: OCHSNER SPORT Zürich Marathon
summary: The Zürich Marathon has been held in April since 2003. It starts at the Quaibrücke, runs through the city and along the shore of Lake Zurich to a turnaround in Meilen, then returns to the city. Since 2025 the finish has been on the Sechseläutenplatz.
courseHighlights: Run along the shore of Lake Zurich

paceStrategy.summary: The courses mostly follow the lake shore, so pacing can be even. The turnaround at Meilen splits the race, and runners must reach it by a cut-off time.

segments.terrain: City centre and the start of the lake shore
segments.advice: Settle into goal pace; the start is a mass start with rolling blocks.
Keep an even pace and reach the Meilen turnaround before its cut-off time.

segments.terrain: Lake shore back towards the city
segments.advice: Hold your pace; split times are recorded at km 30 and 40.
Use the last kilometres to finish strongly.

fuelingNotes: The official site has a separate page on food and drink; read it for aid-station details. On a flat lakeside course, a gel every 30 to 40 minutes is a simple plan.
tips: Be at the start at least one hour before your start time to allow time for bag drop and warm-up
Your start block may be several hundred metres to nearly 2 km from the start line
Timing mats record split times at km 10, 20, 21.1, 30 and 40
The turnaround in Meilen has a cut-off time, so do not start too slowly if you are near the time limit

faq.question: Is the Zurich Marathon flat?
faq.answer: The courses mostly follow the shore of Lake Zurich. The official site has an elevation profile in its route plan, but does not state a single elevation figure in the text.

faq.question: When is the Zurich Marathon held?
faq.answer: It is held on a Sunday in April.

faq.question: Where does the Zurich Marathon turn around?
faq.answer: The turnaround point is in Meilen, on Lake Zurich.
